subject: Deploy path & migration triage for QuantaHealth
messages:
From: Andrew Kim <andrew@quantahealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@quantahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 14:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + demo — follow-up on hosting preferences

Thanks for the demo today, Naomi — good walkthrough. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can move toward procurement: 

Summary: QuantaHealth runs a real-time clinical triage feature (low latency NLP for short prompts) and an offline batch scoring pipeline (embeddings + reranking). We currently have traffic split ~70/30 realtime/batch. We evaluated other hosted LLM APIs and also have an internal GPU cluster (NVIDIA A10s) used for model experiments.

Key priorities:
- Latency: 99th pct target ~220ms for single-turn triage call
- Data controls: PHI scope — need KMS-backed key management and audit logs
- Cost predictability for high-volume batch scoring

Questions:
1) We are leaning toward Dedicated capacity but need to understand the work required to integrate our KMS and to route only PHI traffic to a private environment.
2) Can Redwood accept a phased migration: start with Hosted API for a proof-of-concept (no PHI), then a Dedicated pool, then Private VPC for full PHI?
3) Any experience migrating from other LLM APIs + a self-hosted cluster? Biggest lift we anticipate is KV cache migration and request shaping.

Attached a short requirements doc (QuantaHealth-Requirements.pdf) — covers compliance flags and rough Q2 timeline. Would like to set a follow-up technical call next week.

Thanks,
Andrew
Sr. Product Manager, QuantaHealth

(attachment: QuantaHealth-Requirements.pdf)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Andrew Kim <andrew@quantahealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + demo — follow-up on hosting preferences

Thanks Andrew — great notes and appreciated context. Short answers up front, then proposed next steps.

Short answers:
- KMS / PHI: We support KMS integrations for Dedicated + Private (bring-your-own KMS/HSM). Hosted API can be used with pseudonymized data during POC but we do not recommend PHI on the shared hosted tier. Audit logs and token-level tracing are available on Dedicated/Private.
- Phased migration: Yes — many customers start on Hosted for product validation, move to Dedicated when throughput/latency/cost stabilize, then onboard Private VPC for PHI and compliance. We have a documented phased playbook.
- Migration from other APIs/self-hosted clusters: Common asks are model compatibility, KV cache warming, and request shaping (batching vs single-shot). We provide a Migration Checklist and a small starter automation to seed caches and warm endpoints — attached.

Proposed next steps:
1) Tech deep-dive (60m) with our infra engineer Jonas and your infra lead — suggest Tue 20 Apr, 10:00am PT.
2) Share Redwood-Migration-Checklist.xlsx (attached) for your infra to review; please flag any gaps.
3) I'll open a HubSpot opportunity (linked below) and we can capture expected volume tiers for Dedicated sizing.

I've attached the migration checklist and a short do/don't doc. For the call please have: target QPS/latency SLAs, current GPU cluster specs, and your KMS contact.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

(attachment: Redwood-Migration-Checklist.xlsx)

---
Naomi Feldman
Redwood Inference | Solutions Engineering
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@quantahealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tech deep-dive — KMS & migration constraints

Thanks Naomi and Jonas — call was helpful. A few items summarized for clarity and to confirm assumptions: 

Decisions emerging from call:
- We will run the initial POC on Hosted (non-PHI) for two weeks to validate inference quality and latency under simulated traffic. Goal: validate model choice and end-to-end latency (client→Redwood→response).
- If POC meets thresholds, we will commit to a Dedicated pool (reserve monthly commit) and test KMS integration with a staging key.
- Final move to Private VPC will be gated on SOC2 evidence and a production runbook. Target is Q3 cutover if Dedicated performance matches expectations.

Constraints and asks from our infra team:
- Our internal GPU cluster uses a custom KV cache helper. We'll need guidance for migrating cached embeddings and for seeding KV on Dedicated nodes.
- Is there a recommended approach to keep warm caches during the POC to avoid cold-start latency spikes?

We uploaded a short note about our cache helper to the Drive link Naomi shared. Also adding an expected volume snapshot for April and a rough Q3 projection to the HubSpot record.

Next requests:
1) Can Redwood provide a one-page runbook for cache seeding and for the KMS handoff (who performs rotation, what logs are generated)?
2) Proposed tech review with your infra owner + our SRE on Thu 22 Apr at 9:00am PT — please confirm.

Thanks,
Priya
Engineering Lead, QuantaHealth

(Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c_redwood_quanta_requirements)

Appreciate the clarifications and the call, team — quick summary and concrete next steps so nothing slips.

Summary of plan:
- Week 1 (POC Hosted, non-PHI): Redwood to provision a test API key and apply request shaping rules for single-shot low-latency calls. Redwood will share a small load-testing script for cache warming.
- Week 3 (Dedicated sizing + staging KMS): If POC meets latency/cost targets, we’ll provision a Dedicated pool. We'll run a staged integration with your staging KMS; Jonas will own the KMS handoff steps.
- Q3 (Private VPC cutover): Contingent on SOC2 evidence and runbook signoff; Redwood provides Private VPC templates and support for key rotation via your KMS.

Action items (owners & dates):
- Naomi: Send cache-seeding runbook + load-test script (today) — link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c_redwood_quanta_requirements
- Jonas: Prep Dedicated sizing estimate based on the volume snapshot uploaded to HubSpot (ETA: 2027-05-03) — HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/QUANTA-987
- Priya/Quanta infra: Validate KV cache compatibility and flag custom steps (ETA: 2027-05-05)
- Marissa: Draft a one-page KMS & audit-log runbook and a temporary MSA amendment for Dedicated trials (sending DocuSign link) by 2027-05-04

Attachments included for your reference: Redwood-Migration-Checklist.xlsx (detailed steps), QuantaHealth-Requirements.pdf (from your team).

I'll also create a short canary plan template for Dedicated → Private VPC transition and include rollback criteria. If you confirm the Thu 22 Apr tech review time was fine (we were on the call), we'll proceed with the proposed schedule.

I'll open a HubSpot opportunity and send a DocuSign for the trial amendment so procurement can start routing internally.

Best,
